area_note: PicoRV32 is tiny, about 1-2k flops. Most of it is the 32x32 register file (1024 bits, or 992 without x0). The rest is roughly 5x32 bits of pc, next_pc, op1, op2 and out, 128 bits of counters, decode latches, and about 200 bits of fast-mul state. A 16-word operand buffer (512 bits) is half the register file and roughly a quarter to a third of the core's state, so it is significant. The shipped red_accel template keeps operands[16] plus product_words[16], which is 1024 bits, about the same as the whole register file. It also adds its own 32x32 multiplier, which duplicates the fast_mul array. On this core 'large' means anything at or above 32 words of state, or a second multiplier.
constraints: The core is multi-cycle with CPI of 3 or more. Each instruction costs at least 3 cycles, and a load or store costs 5.
PCPI by itself cannot access memory. It gets rs1 and rs2 and returns one 32-bit rd.
In this harness only, the accelerator can master the bus through the red_core.v mux, and only while busy, with the CPU stalled on pcpi_wait. There is no concurrency with the CPU.
Memory is a single port with no burst or cache, and instruction fetch shares it. Moving one word takes about 2 cycles through the accelerator's handshake.
The accelerator must raise pcpi_wait within 16 cycles of pcpi_valid. Otherwise pcpi_timeout traps the instruction as illegal (CATCH_ILLINSN=1).
At most 2 source registers and 1 destination register per instruction. The only result path to the register file is 32 bits.
Use opcodes custom-0 through custom-3. Never use funct7=0000001 on OP (0110011), which the mul and div units take.
A 32x32 hardware multiplier already exists (fast_mul, about 2-cycle latency). A custom MAC that only replaces MUL plus ADD saves little unless it removes loads and stores or loop overhead.
There is no barrel shifter, so shifts cost 4 to 14 cycles. Shift-heavy inner loops are a real target.
The accelerator must deassert pcpi_ready after one cycle and wait for !pcpi_valid before it accepts the next instruction (see the S_WAIT pattern in red_accel.v).
IRQs are disabled. No interrupt can arrive while the accelerator is running.
coprocessor: PCPI (Pico Co-Processor Interface): pcpi_valid, pcpi_insn[31:0], pcpi_rs1, pcpi_rs2 go out; pcpi_wr, pcpi_rd[31:0], pcpi_wait, pcpi_ready come in. Any instruction the core does not recognise (instr_trap) is sent to PCPI. With dual-port registers, pcpi_valid goes high in cpu_state_ld_rs1 together with both rs1 and rs2. The CPU stalls until pcpi_ready, then writes pcpi_rd to rd if pcpi_wr is set. If pcpi_wait is not raised within 16 cycles (pcpi_timeout_counter), the instruction traps as illegal. Bare PCPI cannot address memory: it only gets two register values and returns one. In this eval harness, red_core.v adds a 1-bit bus mux. While red_accel holds busy, it owns mem_valid, mem_addr, mem_wdata, mem_wstrb and mem_rdata, and cpu_mem_ready is forced to 0. This only works because the CPU is stalled on pcpi_wait. So the accelerator can be a bus master, but only while its own instruction is executing. It cannot run in the background or overlap with the CPU.
coprocessor_result: At most one 32-bit word per instruction, written to rd: pcpi_rd, kept only if pcpi_wr=1 when pcpi_ready=1. Anything wider has to go back to memory through the harness bus-master path (red_core.v mux), or come back over several instructions.
custom_opcode_space: custom-0 0001011 (0x0B). Free because ENABLE_IRQ=0, so the PicoRV32 IRQ instructions (getq/setq/retirq/maskirq/timer, which use custom-0) are not decoded. The red_accel template decodes funct3=000, funct7=0000000 here.
The internal mul and div units claim OP 0110011 with funct7=0000001. Do not use that encoding.

eval/rtl/red_core.v: the bus mux selects acc_* when acc_busy, and cpu_mem_ready = acc_busy ? 0 : mem_ready.

existing_units: Fast multiplier picorv32_pcpi_fast_mul: a single 33x33 signed array multiply (rd <= rs1*rs2), result ready 2 cycles after issue (active[1]) with EXTRA_MUL_FFS=0, so MUL costs about 5 to 6 cycles in total. It is a 32x32->64 hardware multiplier, so do not add a second one unless it is needed for parallelism.
Divider picorv32_pcpi_div: sequential shift-subtract, about 32+ cycles for DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU.
Shifter: no barrel shifter (BARREL_SHIFTER=0). It is an iterative two-stage shifter (by 4, then by 1) in cpu_state_shift.
isa: RV32IM, no C, no IRQ. red_core.v sets ENABLE_FAST_MUL=1 (MUL/MULH/MULHSU/MULHU), ENABLE_DIV=1 (DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU), COMPRESSED_ISA=0, ENABLE_IRQ=0, ENABLE_COUNTERS=1 (rdcycle/rdinstret, 64-bit). It uses the defaults ENABLE_REGS_16_31=1 (32 registers) and CATCH_ILLINSN=1. ENABLE_PCPI is 1 only in the accelerated core.
memory_interface: Native PicoRV32 bus: mem_valid/mem_ready handshake, 32-bit mem_addr, mem_wdata, mem_rdata, and a 4-bit mem_wstrb (0 means read). One transfer at a time. There is no cache, no burst and no outstanding-request queue. Instruction fetch uses the same port (mem_instr). In red_soc_tb.v the memory raises mem_ready one cycle after it sees mem_valid. The red_accel template's mem_issued handshake therefore takes about 2 cycles per word.
microarchitecture: Multi-cycle, not pipelined. One FSM in picorv32.v (cpu_state_fetch, ld_rs1, ld_rs2, exec, shift, stmem, ldmem, trap) runs one instruction at a time. With the default ENABLE_REGS_DUALPORT=1 the documented CPI is about 3 for ALU ops (reg-reg and reg-imm), about 3 for a branch not taken and 5 for a taken one, 5 for loads and stores, and 4 to 14 for shifts (TWO_STAGE_SHIFT=1, BARREL_SHIFTER=0, so 4 bits and then 1 bit per cycle). Because every instruction costs at least 3 cycles, software is slow, and a custom instruction that replaces N instructions saves about 3N cycles or more.
name: PicoRV32 (eval/rtl/red_core.v configuration)
register_file: 32 x 32-bit (x0 hardwired to zero), regfile_size=32 because ENABLE_IRQ=0. ENABLE_REGS_DUALPORT=1 (the default) gives 2 read ports and 1 write port. A custom instruction can therefore take at most 2 register operands (rs1, rs2) and write 1 register (rd). Any more operands must come from memory or from state kept inside the accelerator.
